name: Blue Dart Express Ltd
title: Blue Dart Express Ltd - 526612 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Blue Dart Q1 FY27 revenue rose to INR1,658 crore (from INR1,442 crore) and PAT reached INR87 crore, driven mainly by yield and fuel surcharge rather than volume.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was INR1,658 crore against INR1,442 crore a year earlier, with PAT of INR87 crore. Management attributed growth mainly to pricing: GPI-led increases, targeted repricing of loss-making lanes and customers, and fuel surcharge recovery after diesel and Brent prices rose from around March–May. Tonnage grew about 7% to 364,430 tons and shipments about 2% to 96.15 million, with air volume up about 2.6% and surface up about 9%. Management declined to quantify yield growth or give forward volume and margin guidance, citing seasonality and H2 resourcing challenges.

segments.name: Air
segments.commentary: About 60% of revenue but about 25% of kilos (1:3 air:surface by weight). Volume growth about 2.6%; growth is mainly yield-led. Freighter pallet utilisation 85–90%.

segments.name: Surface / Ground
segments.commentary: About 40% of revenue and about 75% of kilos. Volume up about 9%; B2B revenue up about 14%. Management says surface is the faster-growing segment and is approaching air in size.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: Revenue up more than 10% YoY. Management says about 50-plus million of the 96.15 million shipments are e-commerce, and Blue Dart holds about 12–13% of outsourced/3PL e-commerce.

segments.name: B2B vs B2C
segments.commentary: Revenue mix about 70% B2B and 30% B2C (plus or minus 2%).

segments.name: BFSI (documents and cards)
segments.commentary: BFSI alone is about 10–15% of total revenue; documents plus cards together, including small parcels, about 25–30%. Management says BFSI is no longer a growing segment.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance. Management said it will not forecast volumes, citing seasonality, but expects Q2 to reflect the full fuel-surcharge increase from May onward.
Typical GPI realisation is about 4–5%, with extra customer-specific corrections on top.

Standalone annualised capex guided at INR100–150 crore, mostly replacement and expansion. Aviation capex is driven by maintenance and engine cycles, with roughly 20–25% of depreciation as ongoing capex.
H2 is expected to bring higher volumes, but resourcing flex will determine margins; management aims for stable, consistent margin improvement.
No major expansion plans; growth is expected to be organic. Possible consolidation and expansion of southern hubs (Bangalore, Chennai) and Mumbai, a few quarters away.
capex_capacity: Two major hubs added in North and a couple of medium-sized hubs in East in the prior period.
Freighter pallet utilisation at 85–90%; aircraft flown mainly at night and scheduled against available load.
Belly cargo is 30–40% of overall load in a typical month, and can reach 70–80% on lower-volume weekends. Blue Dart flies to 8 stations and carries belly cargo at 25–50 other locations.
The two aircraft acquired earlier are back to pre-acquisition pallet utilisation (as of 2024) and are integrated into the network.
demand_pricing: Growth came mainly from pricing: GPI increases, repricing of loss-making lanes and customers, and fuel surcharge pass-through. Management said yield was 'directionally' the main driver of revenue growth.
Fuel surcharge on surface is revised monthly based on local diesel prices, which rose in mid-May after about 5–6 years. Air fuel surcharge rose from April as Brent climbed from around mid-March.
Auto is a niche express vertical; management estimates it grows at about high-teens, in line with surface B2B. Market share is hard to quantify.
Management says e-commerce pricing remains competitive, with capacity still available in the market; Blue Dart positions itself as a premium player.
Management says it gained a very small but roughly stable market share in SME clients versus last year (informal assessment).

qa_highlights.question: Is the revenue growth mainly from pricing, given volume growth was only about 7%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed directionally. Pricing came from GPI increases, repricing of loss-making lanes and customers, and fuel surcharge recovery (fuel surcharge offset fuel cost rises, which also lifted yield).

qa_highlights.question: Why is e-commerce growth lower than the industry, and is it a focus area?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said e-commerce is a growth driver but not a mass-volume focus. It is prioritising premium, time-critical traffic that fits its capacity, and it is not targeting the largest e-commerce share.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex plans and new hubs?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone annualised capex is INR100–150 crore, mostly replacement and expansion. Two major northern hubs and some medium eastern hubs were added, and southern and Mumbai hub consolidation is being considered a few quarters away.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are margins, and what is the H2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 brings volume opportunity but also resourcing challenges. It aims to keep or improve margins through efficiency and better realisation, without quantifying either.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 2 recently acquired aircraft stabilised?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said pallet utilisation was restored to pre-acquisition levels by 2024. The aircraft are part of the wider network, and capacity is not a constraint; yield is the main lever.

risks_watch: Growth quality: about 7% tonnage growth against about 15% revenue growth implies most of the increase came from pricing and surcharges, which may not persist.
Fuel: diesel and Brent rises were passed through with a lag; Q2 is expected to show the full surcharge effect, but any fall in fuel prices would reverse it.
Air volume growth of about 2.6% versus surface about 9% suggests air is stagnating in volume.
H2 resourcing: management flagged that peak-season flex will decide margins.
Competition in e-commerce pricing remains intense, with spare capacity in the market.
BFSI (documents and cards) is no longer growing, and the 25–30% documents-plus-parcels exposure needs monitoring.
Management declined to provide e-commerce split by air and surface, D2C share, or yield premium figures, limiting visibility.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter's numbers and direction, but guarded on forward-looking detail: it declined to quantify yield, the e-commerce premium, and market share, and repeatedly deferred to seasonality rather than guiding.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR1,442 crore in Q1 FY26 (about +15%)
